original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Masked (E-graph) exactness with eight costly terms: real K on the live lines with K_ii = 4, K_ij = 0 on orthogonal live pairs, odd entries free, rank K <= 8. Exact infinitesimal rigidity of this solution set at K0 = 2G on P120, P112 and all 1260 frame-pair punctures P104 = P120 - F0 - F1 (three classes under explicit stabilizer elements), plus a seeded exact sample of 64 random punctures with 24 to 80 lines.
scope_change_reason: Before synthesizing a masked decoder, test whether masking can deform the cheapest known decoders at all. The changed assumption is the all-pairs exactness of the eight-term bound (odd entries become free); the frame-pair punctures attain the 7/13 copy ratio, so they are where a masked deformation would matter first.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. A masked deformation of the frame-pair decoder with smaller supports would lower the copy charge below the 7/13 ratio. Local rigidity shows that no such deformation exists near the all-pairs normal form, so any masked gain at P104 must come from a separate solution component.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact tangent certificate covers every frame-pair class, or after the first exact non-torus tangent direction (which would become the lead). No global solution-set search was attempted within the budget.
evidence: verify.py: 9 exact checks. rank over F_p (p = 2^31 - 1) of the masked tangent system is 7v - 63 and the explicit gauge plus torus directions span 64 + v - 1, so the tangent space of the solution set equals the torus tangent (dimension v - 1) for P120, P112 and the three P104 classes (896, 336 and 28 frames); a decomposable D4 + D4 live set is rejected; 64 of 64 seeded deeper punctures pass.
author: Navinor
ai_assistance: Prepared with help from opencode (research, implementation and documentation).

open_questions.question: Is the masked rank-8 solution set on each P104 frame-pair puncture globally equal to the torus orbit of 2G?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An off-orbit component could have smaller term supports than the frame-pair decoder and beat the 7/13 copy ratio; local rigidity cannot exclude it.
open_questions.first_step: Pivot on a live frame F (the mask forces K[F,F] = 4I, so K = K[:,F] K[F,:] / 4) and solve the resulting bilinear system class by class for the three frame-pair classes.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a written case analysis comparable to the P112/P120 global proof in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1212; not started here.

open_questions.question: Do nine or more costly terms with masked exactness admit cheaper decoders on P104?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the mixed-beta problem of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717 moved to the ratio-optimal puncture; rank-8 rigidity does not constrain rank-9 costly parts.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the tangent computation at rank 9 for a fixed ninth support pattern on one P104 class.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a chosen support alphabet for the ninth term; no candidate is proposed here.
